correctness.rationale: Proof independently reconstructs the Fourier kernel for the two affine-equivalence classes from inclusion-exclusion. The counted Fourier coefficients give exact sharp complex l-infinity convolution norm, attained by a conjugate phase input. The q=2 normalization is checked separately. Additive-character second-moment identities yield rigorous Cauchy-Schwarz inequalities; the difference polynomial is positive from q=4, and q=3 has explicit positive gap (11-6 sqrt(3))/9. Fixed-p limit follows from the root-of-unity sums. The standalone checker tests 9 prime/extension fields canonically and all 3,256 three-direction affine arrangements in fields of size 2,3,4,5; finite tests support but do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: A three-line transverse affine arrangement is the first natural small configuration that distinguishes concurrent and nonconcurrent incidence geometry. Its Fourier algebra norm is a sharp and useful endpoint stability invariant, and the theorem completely classifies this invariant for every finite field, proves the strict order with a binary reversal, and evaluates arithmetic prime-power limits. This is a motivated structural boundary, not an arbitrary small-table computation or rediscovery of the known three-step-walk constant.
